description: Answer key for retrieval: realistic complaints and the rule section(s) that clearly govern them. A retrieved passage counts if its section matches (official interpretations of that section also count).

scenarios.issue: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account
scenarios.complaint: Two debit card transactions I never made appeared on my checking account. I told the bank the same day but they say I am responsible for the money.
I reported an error on my bank statement over a month ago and the bank still has not finished its investigation or put the money back in my account.

scenarios.issue: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account
scenarios.complaint: My debit card was stolen and I waited about a week to tell my bank. Now they say I have to cover all the fraudulent ATM withdrawals.
My bank charged me overdraft fees on everyday debit card purchases even though I never agreed to overdraft coverage.
The bank raised the monthly maintenance fee on my savings account without telling me in advance.
When I opened my checking account the bank never gave me any written list of the fees and the interest rate terms.
I sent money to my family abroad through a transfer company and they received less than the amount I was promised. The company refuses to fix it.
I tried to cancel an international money transfer twenty minutes after I paid for it, but the provider refused to cancel or refund it.

scenarios.issue: Unauthorized transactions or other transaction problem
scenarios.complaint: Someone used my prepaid card for purchases I did not make, and the card company refuses to investigate because I never registered the card.

scenarios.issue: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
scenarios.complaint: I disputed a charge on my credit card statement for an item that was never delivered, and the card issuer never responded to my letter.

scenarios.issue: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
scenarios.complaint: My credit card was used fraudulently and the issuer is holding me liable for over a thousand dollars of charges I did not make.
My credit card company raised my interest rate without giving me any advance notice.
I was charged a 41 dollar late fee even though my payment was one day late and my minimum payment was only 25 dollars.
I paid more than the minimum on my credit card, but the extra was applied to the balance with the lowest interest rate instead of the highest.
I sent my mortgage servicer a written notice that they misapplied my payments, and they never corrected it or replied.
I asked my mortgage servicer in writing for my payment history and the name of the owner of my loan and never got an answer.
My escrow payment went up sharply and the servicer never sent me an escrow account statement explaining the shortage.
I submitted a complete loan modification application, but the servicer started foreclosure on my home anyway.
My servicer bought expensive homeowners insurance and charged it to my loan even though I already had my own insurance policy.
My mortgage payment arrived on time, but the servicer did not credit it until several days later and charged me a late fee.
I disputed an account on my credit report that is not mine and the credit bureau did not remove it or finish an investigation within 30 days.
I am a victim of identity theft and want the fraudulent accounts blocked from my credit report, but the credit bureau refuses.

scenarios.issue: Credit monitoring or identity theft protection services
scenarios.complaint: I asked the credit bureau to put a fraud alert on my file after my wallet was stolen, and they never did.
A company pulled my credit report and created a hard inquiry even though I never applied for anything with them.
A collection account from more than ten years ago is still showing on my credit report.
I disputed wrong information directly with my credit card company, which reports to the bureaus, and they keep reporting the same wrong information.
A debt collector contacted me about a debt I don't recognize and never sent me any written notice explaining the debt or how to dispute it.
A debt collector calls me eight times a day and uses abusive language when I answer.
A debt collector keeps calling me at work even after I told them my employer does not allow these calls.

scenarios.issue: Threatened to contact someone or share information improperly
scenarios.complaint: The debt collector threatened that I would be arrested if I did not pay the full amount today.

scenarios.issue: Took or threatened to take negative or legal action
scenarios.complaint: A collector sued me over a credit card debt that is more than ten years old, well past the statute of limitations.
When I financed my car, the dealer never clearly showed me the APR and the total finance charge before I signed.
My private student loan lender never gave me the required disclosures about the interest rate and loan terms before I accepted the loan.
My personal loan contract did not show the annual percentage rate or the total of payments anywhere.
